correctness.rationale: Weyl integration of ordinary SU(2) trace characters gives ||chi_m||_6^6=(m+1)(m²+2m+2)/2; Clebsch-Gordan fusion independently verified this exact identity for m=0..31. For each fixed finite S, on theta<=pi/2, chi_(m+s)-chi_m is uniformly bounded by O(s), because |sin((m+s+1)theta)-sin((m+1)theta)| <=s theta. The reflected endpoint has parity signs (-1)^s. Weighted L5 size of chi_m is O(m²), so replacing the packet on each half by (A+B)chi_m and (A-B)chi_m gives a uniform O_S(m²) error and leading m³/4 (|A+B|^6+|A-B|^6). Cauchy-Schwarz saturates only for constant profiles in each active parity class; relative phases are 0 or pi. With a=max(e,o),b=min(e,o), the energy split p yields cubic Phi=1/2(q³+12ab q p(1-p)), q=ap+b(1-p). Its derivative in Bernstein form has unique interior zero for 1<=a/b<5 and is positive to p=1 for a/b>=5. Uniform convergence on compact unit coefficient sphere yields convergence of finite-weight maximizers to the complete limiting equality set. Exactly fixed supports only, no growing-bandwidth claim.

value.rationale: The L²-to-L6 extremizer of a high highest-weight central character packet is a natural sparse representation-theoretic synthesis problem. The threshold a/b=5 is a sharp concentration/mixing phase transition with full coefficient phase classification and parity-count universality, different from the known fourth-moment 3:1 phase transition. Supports with (4,1) versus (5,1) expose a motivated boundary not mechanically implied by the single- or two-character moment.
